vulnerability.title: Shutdown System When Auditing Failures Occur
vulnerability.description: If the auditd daemon is configured to use the augenrules program to read audit rules during daemon startup (the default), add the following line to to the bottom of a file with suffix .rules in the directory /etc/audit/rules.d: -f If the auditd daemon is configured to use the auditctl utility to read audit rules during daemon startup, add the following line to the bottom of the /etc/audit/audit.rules file: -f
vulnerability.recommendation: Remediation script: # Remediation is applicable only in certain platforms if rpm --quiet -q audit && rpm --quiet -q kernel-core; then var_audit_failure_mode='' # Traverse all of: # # /etc/audit/audit.rules, (for auditctl case) # /etc/audit/rules.d/*.rules (for augenrules case) find /etc/audit /etc/audit/rules.d -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*.rules' -exec sed -i '/-f[[:space:]]\+.*/d' {} ';' for AUDIT_FILE in "/etc/audit/audit.rules" "/etc/audit/rules.d/immutable.rules" do echo '' >> $AUDIT_FILE echo '# Set the audit.rules configuration to halt system upon audit failure per security requirements' >> $AUDIT_FILE echo "-f $var_audit_failure_mode" >> $AUDIT_FILE done else >&2 echo 'Remediation is not applicable, nothing was done' fi

triage_decision.reason: Adding the '-f' option to audit rules is a standard STIG hardening step that configures auditd to halt the system on audit failures; it does not affect authentication, networking, or filesystem configuration and is unlikely to cause lockout.
triage_decision.estimated_impact: Audit failure mode may halt the system if auditd encounters errors

previous_review_verdicts.feedback: The plan correctly appends the '-f' option to the relevant audit rule files when it is not already present, which fulfills the STIG requirement of halting the system on audit failures. It is functional and reversible. Minor refinements would improve reliability and clarity.
concerns: The plan will blindly append '-f' to any file named *.rules, including those that might be autogenerated or contain other administrative settings; this could introduce unexpected behavior. The check for an existing '-f' line is basic and may miss variations such as '-f ' with trailing spaces or comments on the same line. The script does not trigger a reload of auditd after updating rules, which may delay the enforcement of the new setting.

If auditd is configured to use the augenrules system, modifying multiple .rules files may not be necessary; typically a single '-f' entry in a dedicated rules file (e.g., immutable.rules) suffices. Adding it to every .rules file may clutter configuration and may not be interpreted if the file is excluded from loading.
